theme: Humanity is fundamentally good and worth trusting.

messages.body: I really do think people are good at heart — look how strangers help each other in a crisis.
Crisis altruism is real, but the data on everyday selfishness is just as real. I'd stay neutral.
Agreed with 01! Trust begets trust. We should lean into believing the best in people.
Honestly that's naive. History is a parade of cruelty the moment no one is watching.
I want to believe it, but I keep thinking: are people good, or just constrained by systems that force it?
Compassion is the default when people feel safe. The proposition holds for me.
The more I sit with it, the less sure I am — maybe we default to self-interest and cruelty when unwatched.
05 raises a fair point. I'm moving toward the fence on this.
